catalog_quote: In Puare, a language of the Serra Hills group, (see figure 2 in 1.4) the following factors are relevant to a description of the tonal system: • there are five underlying tone melodies, L, H, LH, HL and HLH; • the sequence *HLH may not be realised on a single syllable, but only spread over multiple syllables (this limits the number of contrasts on monosyllables to four); • with complex tones there is an additional contrast in the placement of an accent in the word, anywhere in the final two syllables of the phonological word. [p.68] While not identical to the Skou system, the variation is minimal. ... [Table 57, Puare column:] Underlying melodies L, H, LH, HL, LHL; Monosyllabic contrasts L, H, LH, HL; Accent domain …[σσ]#; Accent/Tone cooccurrence LH, HL, LHL. ... it is unlikely to be very divergent from something involving five or possible six tone melodies associated with word-level phonological units, contrastive accent placement on the last two syllables of the phonological word, and a restriction on the appearance of overly complex tonal units on single syllables. [Donohue 2003, App. 2, p.361] The system of Puare, when examined in the light of polysyllabic words, also demonstrates a HLH melody, and we also find evidence for the same sort of accentual phenomenon present in the final two syllables that has been demonstrated for Skou

new_statements.rule_in_words: Puare is a word-tone language (five melodies L, H, LH, HL, HLH assigned to the phonological word). There is no fixed stress; instead, for words bearing complex (contour) melodies, the position of an accent is lexically contrastive within a two-syllable window at the right edge of the phonological word (penult or final; Table 57: accent domain..[σσ]#, co-occurring with LH, HL, LHL). Simple L or H words carry no accent contrast. Donohue 2003 (Appendix 2, ms p.361) independently repeats that Puare polysyllables show 'the same sort of accentual phenomenon present in the final two syllables that has been demonstrated for Skou'.
new_statements.exceptions: Accent contrast exists only with complex tone melodies (not with level L or H); *HLH cannot be realised on a monosyllable. Author flags the comparison as brief and based on survey data ('for which we have adequate data'; Sumo less well documented than Puare).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word (tone melodies and the accent window are word-level; right-dominant tone in compounds is said to hold across the family). Statement is a comparative excursus inside a grammar of Skou, resting on Donohue's own 2000 north-coast survey of Puare (ISO CR 2008-031), not on a dedicated Puare description; no Puare examples with accent marked are given in the excursus (appendix 5.2 wordlists give Chao-letter pitch per item only).
new_statements.identity_note: The statement is explicitly about Puare (Serra Hills group) = puar1240 [pux] (older name Puari; insider name Bkwala; villages Puare/Pino, Sandaun Province), based on Mark Donohue's 2000 coastal survey. It appears as a comparative excursus inside a grammar of a different language, Skou (skou1240), and is repeated in Donohue 2003 (Skou tone paper, Appendix 2). No dedicated grammar or phonology of Puare exists (Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description = wordlist or less).

sources.note: Puare (from Donohue's own 2000 survey data) has five word-level tone melodies L, H, LH, HL, HLH; *HLH cannot sit on one syllable (four monosyllabic contrasts); 'with complex tones there is an additional contrast in the placement of an accent in the word, anywhere in the final two syllables of the phonological word'; Table 57 gives Puare accent domain..[σσ]#, accent/tone co-occurrence LH, HL, LHL.
